video_title: Patrick Peterson REVEALS How He Knew NFL Routes Before They Happened

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on being targeted 22 times by Calvin Johnson
quotes.excerpt: I got targeted 22 times. That's probably your highest activity you ever had in your career.
quotes.quote: My first time going up against Calvin Johnson, I got targeted 22 times. That's probably your highest activity you ever had in your career, by far.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on Eli Manning's hand signals
quotes.excerpt: He used the same hand signal as Eli Manning. I watched tape. I already knew that was a go ball.
quotes.quote: We were playing the New York Giants, I can't remember the year, but he used the same hand signal as Eli Manning. I watched tape. I already knew that was a go ball. So I ran the route for him and the quarterback threw the ball out of bounds. And Eli Manning happened to be there. I said, 'Eli, tell him to change up the signal, man. I watch tape, man. I already knew that was a go ball.'

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his grandmother's advice about his potential
quotes.excerpt: My grandmother used to always tell me this, 'You're going to be something, Pat. Don't waste it.'
quotes.quote: My grandmother used to always tell me this, 'You're going to be something, Pat. Don't waste it.' That's how I took it to heart. I wanted to show them whatever you put your mind to, that you work towards, whatever you want to work towards, it's more than feasible.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his upbringing in Pompano Beach
quotes.excerpt: I'm the oldest of five, so I always had to move differently. I had to lead the right way.
quotes.quote: I'm the oldest of five, so I always had to move differently. I had to lead the right way because I had four of the siblings watching my every move. So I really took that to heart. I really wanted to show them whatever you put your mind to, that you work towards, whatever you want to work towards, it's more than feasible.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his responsibility as the oldest sibling
quotes.excerpt: I had a special talent, I had something that could take me places, so I had to make sure.
quotes.quote: I had a special talent, I had something that could take me places, so I had to make sure I did everything that I needed to do on my end to fulfill whatever dreams and goals I had for myself.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his grandparents' influence
quotes.excerpt: My grandparents used to always tell me, 'God put you in positions for a reason.'
quotes.quote: My grandparents used to always tell me, 'God put you in positions for a reason.' They put people there because He knows that they can handle certain situations. And honestly, I took it like a badge of honor being the oldest. My parents had me young. It's been times where I'm at the house watching the kids, getting dinner ready. Things like that at 10, 11 years old. So I believe I took it as a badge of honor because my last grandparent who is with me to this day, Arthur Johnson, he kind of raised me. That's my mom's dad, so he kind of raised me and just some of the things he used to always tell me, watching how he treated his wife, watching how he conducted his business, watching how his mannerisms around when everything gets chaotic, he's always just chill, because at the end of the day, life is going to life, you just have to know how to maneuver through it.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on the importance of being a professional
quotes.excerpt: You really got to have the total package if you really want to be something great.
quotes.quote: You really got to have the total package if you really want to be something great. Meaning, you got to handle your business on and off the field at all times.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson explains the origin of his last name
quotes.excerpt: That's how Peterson came about because they wasn't married then.
quotes.quote: My mom was a junior in high school, my dad had just got out of high school, so he was basically a freshman in college. And I come around. So in my mom's household, especially with her having me at a young age, there was like, we don't know if you're going to be with him down the road, so he came out of you. That's how Peterson came about because they wasn't married then. So then later on when I was in high school, my junior year, they got married.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson recounts playing under a fake identity in high school
quotes.excerpt: They put me in number 12, I had a dark shield, and was out there still cooking.
quotes.quote: My freshman year, I got suspended, and this wasn't nothing I did outside of football. I celebrated, I did an excessive celebration in the game before. I was supposed to be suspended for the next game coming up, but it was against our rival, Dillard. So our head coach comes into the team meeting room, he's like, 'Man, Pat, they just suspended you, but you're still going to play.' I'm like, 'I'm still going to play? How I'm still going to play?' They put me in number 12, I had a dark shield, and was out there still cooking. So the principal was out there, it's like, 'Hey man, who is that number 12? Where he come from? We ain't seen him the whole year.' A new number 12. Custom player. Basically. Had to wear sleeves, had to look different. So that ended up happening. So he ended up getting fired.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson reflects on his recruitment process by Pete Carroll
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to go to USC, what Pete Carroll had. I never forget when I came down there.
quotes.quote: I wanted to go to USC, what Pete Carroll had. I never forget when I came down there for my, well I came to two visits, the Rising Star that they used to have in the summertime, that was like my initiation of meeting the coaching staff and things like that. Ken Norton, that's my guy, he was the guy who recruited me. So I go there in the summertime, the Rising Star, win MVP, meet Reggie Bush, just kicking it. Going into my senior year, that was my first time actually being on a flight too. That's a five hour flight from Florida, that's a long way away. Pete Carroll on me heavy. Pete Carroll came down to Florida when they gave me my day to the city. I still got pictures of Pete Carroll, Ken Norton and Pat in the audience, watching me receive my keys to the city. I felt like we had a real close connection.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Concerns over USC probation and Pete Carroll's NFL departure
quotes.excerpt: I don't think that's going to be the best pick for me because it's far away.
quotes.quote: All the stuff started coming out about possibly the team going to go on probation, not going to be able to play in bowl games. Pete Carroll's name started floating around in the NFL. So I'm like, that's going to be kind of tough. I get there, you can't play in no bowl games. Pete Carroll might not be there, the guy who I grew a relationship with, who I grew a connection with, who I want to have coach me, because he's a DB guy, I love his energy. I never forget going into the team meeting room, him and the guys, they make this big pile of chairs, they just started throwing chairs in the meeting room. It was like, man, this is what I want to be around. Trusting my instinct, I was like, I don't think that's going to be the best pick for me because it's far away, there's a lot of questions about the school, far as they going to be able to play in bowl games, if Pete Carroll is going to be there. Let me kind of pull the audible, because I literally, I was very, very close to going to USC.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his first visit to LSU
quotes.excerpt: I can't see myself wearing no dang on purple and gold. No, it ain't happening.
quotes.quote: I go to LSU, never had a conversation with LSU until October of my senior year. They invited me out to come to a game. You know, I see LSU every once in a while, you know, being, you know, from Florida. Didn't know much about the school for the most part, but it was at the time, they was about to win a national championship. So I'm like, let me go, let me go check it out. I never forget, man, I go there, I tell my mom, I was like, 'Man, I can't see myself wearing no dang on purple and gold.' Like, no, it ain't happening. But when I went there, man, and just the vibe, the attitude that the players had, I really felt like it was at home. Like the guys, the the the grind that they put in and the same mindset that they had towards football and the attitude they had towards football, I was like, man, I think I probably can get jiggy with this. And it was going to be a fresh slate for me to get there, because all the seniors, Jarvis Jackson, all those guys were out of there. So it was going to be a good opportunity for me and what really rung my bell, they never had a Jim Thorpe winner. And I always, you know, I always had dreams of being in this position, like no bull crap. So I know you're probably going to get to this question, when did I know? I always knew. Like to be honest with you, like I always knew.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his early success at LSU
quotes.excerpt: My first practice at LSU, I go up against Brandon LaFell. He runs a dig, I knock it down.
quotes.quote: My first practice at LSU, I go up against Brandon LaFell. He runs a dig, I knock it down. He end up running like a slant the next the next time I knock it down that I go against Chris Tolliver, get an interception. Like this is our first time going up against the older guys, because you know how it is with freshmen, like you have your days, you know, you're going to have your field, we want you to learn the system first before you we put you out there with the big boys. Exactly, so my first time out there with the big boys, shoot, I was out there strapping. Man, Brandon LaFell was hot. He was like, 'How we going to let this rookie, this freshman come in here?' So he called me out. My first time going up against Calvin Johnson, I got targeted 22 times. I got targeted 22 times. I got targeted 22 times. He caught 10. That's good, that's 50%. I mean that's Calvin. I had a pick. Yeah, yeah, yeah. That's a solid game. That's a solid game. 22 targets, less than 50%. I mean that's Calvin. I got targeted 22 times.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his first NFL game against Julio Jones
quotes.excerpt: We played Julio Jones, you know, Matt Ryan, was Roddy White still there? Yeah, Roddy was there.
quotes.quote: We played Julio Jones, you know, Matt Ryan, was Roddy White still there? Yeah, Roddy was there, and they was rolling at the time. And Julio Jones gave me my worst game of my career. Julio almost caught everybody at least one time. Man, I was like, he gave me my worst game ever in my NFL career. And it was just all straight comebacks. Literally ran, and he fast too, and he fast too. He called nine 18 yard comebacks the entire game. And then just turned the middle. No, I would, it was like, and he was making great catches like just out of bounds. Like some of them may have been longer than 18 yards, but they was all comebacks on the sideline for the most part. It wasn't nothing like, oh, a straight up go, or a dig, or a slant or anything like that. They was literally all comebacks.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Using ball placement on the hash to predict receiver routes
quotes.excerpt: It all predicates off where the ball is.
quotes.quote: Terrell Arnold called me the other day. He said, 'Man, how did you jump that dig route when y'all was in cover three?' I said, 'Bro, I knew it was coming.' It all predicates off where the ball is. If the ball is further away from you, nine times out of ten you're going to get in-breaking routes, everything back into the quarterback's vision. If you're to the near hash, and you're that DB short side, you only going to get a couple routes. Speed outs, maybe a deep out, and a drag.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Defensive backs using receiver splits to eliminate route possibilities
quotes.excerpt: The receiver is telling you at least four routes that they're possibly going to run.
quotes.quote: Once I figured out figuring out what a ball is on the hash and the splits, now I started a process of elimination. Because at the end of the day, that's what a defensive back is doing. You're not supposed to cover the whole route tree. The receiver is telling you at least four routes that they're possibly going to run due to where the ball is and how their split is. If you're able to watch film and figure that out, that's when you're going to be able to put yourself in better position to make plays.

quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on his transition to becoming a college football analyst
quotes.excerpt: the film study in college ball now is so different, man, because they do so much unorthodox stuff

text_blocks.speaker: Brice Butler
text_blocks.text: Now you're done playing football, now you're on TV as an analyst. How has a lifetime of film study helped that transition feel so natural for you?

text_blocks.speaker: Patrick Peterson
text_blocks.text: It's been different for me this year because I have to do a lot of film study on college ball. The film study in college ball now is so different, man, because they do so much unorthodox stuff. I would never have my quarterback throw the ball from the opposite hash and he's throwing an out route all the way down to the 15-yard out.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson

quotes.quote: I had the opportunity to bring that into the broadcast because many people may not even know that. Duplessis played for Liberty and he goes to school to study whales. I thought that was pretty cool and I had the opportunity to bring that into the broadcast because many people may not even know that. It's pretty cool having the opportunity to bring these players to life for people.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on providing coaching insights to fans during broadcasts
quotes.excerpt: the fans want to hear this stuff. What is the coach going to say on the sideline?

text_blocks.speaker: Patrick Peterson
text_blocks.text: The fans want to hear this stuff. What is the coach going to say after this kid just gave up an 80-yard bomb? What is he saying to him on the sideline? What are the coaching points? They're just at home, never played football, just watching the game, but giving them that insight makes them become a bigger fan.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson

Nobody is saying no to an LSU job. 13-point whatever a year, second highest paid college head football coach, giving you $25 million to spend when you already have a program to where you have to go into the transfer portal to get players.

quotes.quote: Everybody is trying to upgrade. So what is the problem with Lane Kiffin going to get an upgrade? Everybody's phone got an upgrade. Everybody is trying to upgrade. So what is the problem with Lane Kiffin going to get an upgrade? He felt like this was a great opportunity for him to do less transfer portals, have $25 million to spend, and he's the second highest paid coach in college football.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Peterson on the importance of being true to oneself

quotes.quote: You have to really stick by it. Be true to yourself. You have to be true to yourself, look yourself in the mirror, and give yourself honest answers. Was I my best today? Am I doing my best? What can I do to get better? You have to be honest with yourself.
